chunks: Regarding the man who strikes the hunted prey and cuts it in two halves — he said: He may eat both of them together. But if he struck it and a part was cut off from it, he should not eat from it what was cut off, and he may eat the rest of it.

key_terms.أبان: Severed/cut off — used in fiqh to describe the separation of a part from the main body
key_terms.الصيد: Hunted game — an animal hunted using a weapon or hunting tool; its permissibility depends on proper conditions including the hunter's intention and the nature of the kill
key_terms.عضو: Limb/member — a part or appendage of an animal's body that has been severed from the whole
key_terms.يقده: Cutting/splitting the prey — the act of severing the prey in two with the weapon at the moment of the killing strike

ai.seo_question: If a hunter's arrow or weapon cuts the prey in two, can he eat both halves in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a legal ruling on the permissibility of consuming hunted game that has been split into two halves by the hunter's strike. If the prey is cleanly cut in two at the moment of the lethal blow, both halves are permissible to eat. However, if a limb or part is severed separately from the main body during the hunt, that severed part is forbidden while the rest of the carcass remains permissible. This distinction reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that a part severed from a living animal — or in this case severed during the hunt without being the killing blow — is treated as a separate piece requiring its own proper slaughter conditions.
